description:
Found while building fz-sc8.8. Reproduces on b870f5a87 (fz-sc8.18 head), so it predates .8.

Observed, with `fz2 run` and the binary from `fz2 build` behaving the same:

    def main(), do: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}                exit 0
    def main(), do: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}             exit 138
    def main(), do: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}          exit 138
    def main(), do: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}       exit 0
    def main(), do: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9}    exit 139
    def main(), do: {1, 2, {2, 3, 4, 5}}           exit 138   (nested: six scalar lanes)
    def main(), do: {1, 2, {2, 3, 4}}              exit 0     (five lanes)
    def main(), do: [1, 2, {3, 4, 5, 6}]           exit 0     (a list, not a tuple)
    def f(), do: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}; def main(), do: f()                   exit 138
    def f(), do: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}; def main() do {a,_,_,_,_,f} = f(); a + f end   exit 0

So a six-lane tuple survives a call between fz functions; what fails is the ROOT returning it (main's own return reaching the driver). `fz2 interp` exits 0 on every line. The types dump shows `main/0[] => {int, int, int, int, int, int}`.


It was masked until .8 because `dbg/1` returned through an `any` extern; with .8 `fixtures2/behavior/anonymous_fn_bare_params` ends main in a six-lane `dbg({...})` and goes red on run and build. Repro files: session scratchpad p8/bugA/ (a1..a10, b1..b9, c5..c9).

Blocks fz-sc8.8. Fix lands first, on its own branch above fz-sc8.18. Root cause and fix: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.97.html (the root return layout publishes N unboxed lanes while the halt continuation takes one word; the root return becomes a one-word boundary in the transport predicate that already does this for any-typed extern positions). The earlier "build only, exit 134" dbg symptom was a snapshot binary linking a rebuilt runtime archive, not a bug.
title: A root main returning a tuple of six or more lanes crashes the JIT and the native build
